notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a useful architectural note about useContent being the central hub for 236+ components. I built the entire AC set from the story title, description, file list, and that architectural insight. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 separate the general real-time update requirement from component-type-specific coverage to make testability granular. (2) AC-3/AC-9/AC-14 form a three-layer safety net ensuring production never sees preview data, connections, or bundle weight. (3) AC-4/AC-5/AC-13 cover error/resilience scenarios — connection loss, recovery, and malformed data. (4) AC-6 addresses the initial-load race condition (published content first, then preview overlay). (5) AC-7 is the no-regression gate for the 236+ existing consumers of useContent. (6) AC-8 covers nested references since Contentstack entries commonly reference other entries. (7) AC-10 ensures cross-codebase parity since the story explicitly scopes GO, UP, MX. (8) AC-11 addresses concurrent edits. (9) AC-12 covers session resumption. (10) AC-15 covers the publish-transition lifecycle. CAVEAT: Without file contents I could not verify existing useContent signatures, return types, or how contentstack.ts currently initializes the SDK — these ACs may need refinement once the current API surface is known, particularly around how preview data is expected to merge with or replace published data.

notes: Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria for this story, so all 14 criteria were derived from the story title, description ('[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS'), and the technical file context (useContent hook, Contentstack service, ContentstackContext, and downstream consumers). Criteria cover: preview-mode activation and draft content serving (AC1), real-time update without reload (AC2), automatic downstream consumer benefit without code changes (AC3), production isolation with no behavioral regression (AC4), graceful degradation on SDK init failure (AC5), SSR/build safety (AC6), malformed update resilience (AC7), multi-codeline consistency across gotransit/upexpress/metrolinx (AC8), resource cleanup on unmount (AC9), performance under rapid updates (AC10), content sanitization parity (AC11), field-level editability metadata for CMS inline editing (AC12), accessibility non-interference (AC13), and configuration gating when preview credentials are absent (AC14). File contents for the five listed files were not available in this review; reviewing the actual implementations of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, and ContentstackContext.tsx would allow refinement of AC5 (specific failure modes), AC9 (exact cleanup verification), and AC12 (what metadata format the CMS expects). The story description is extremely terse — '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS' — which limits precision around expected latency thresholds, supported content types, and whether inline editing (not just live preview) is in scope.
